candidates.title: Break and recover four M2.5 HELICOIL tangs from an ODRI actuator shell base
candidates.objective: Finish four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a representative ODRI actuator shell base: align and hold the specified straight tang break-off mandrel in each insert, strike it with a separately manipulated hammer to fracture the tang at its manufactured notch, then physically recover every released tang into a tray without damaging the retained inserts or shell.
skills: precision grasping of a narrow mandrel
coaxial alignment with recessed M2.5 inserts
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires four contact-loaded fractures at the modeled notches, four independently simulated free tangs physically deposited in a containment tray, no tang remaining in or escaping from the shell, every insert retained within frozen pose tolerances, no shell or coil damage, all tools released, and a two-second stable final state. Partial credit may cover safe alignment or fewer completed fractures only while every released fragment remains contained. Insufficient or repeated impacts, glancing blows, off-axis overload, insert displacement, shell damage, tool jamming, fragment loss, or any pose/velocity injection invalidates full success.
candidates.industrial_value: The pinned ODRI robot-actuator procedure requires four M2.5 × 3.75 mm inserts in the shell base, removal of their tangs, and verification that tangs do not remain inside the part. Böllhoff documents notch fracture and identifies the M2.5 straight tang break-off mandrel.
candidates.dexterity: One arm must maintain a narrow mandrel coaxially inside a small recessed insert while the other delivers a controlled hammer impact. The robot must avoid lateral loading of the retained coil and printed boss, withdraw the mandrel without snagging, and recover four small loose metal fragments from an open shell cavity.

candidates.asset_plan: Build an independently authored representative rigid fixture rather than claiming an exact current-product replica. The four inspected pinned ODRI images establish four marked shell-base insert bosses, vertical installation access, the open cavity and large through-openings, and completed inserts. Use the documented M2.5 × 3.75 mm insert and Böllhoff M2.5 mandrel family to anchor the local interaction. Treat the historical unitless STL and 2019 v1 overview only as explicitly outdated geometry references. Model retained coil proxies, separate tangs, manufactured notches, mandrel, hammer, shell, and tray as native rigid PhysX bodies. Freeze and disclose uncited wire, notch, handle, friction, fracture-load, impulse, damage, and tolerance values as prototype assumptions. Before YAM integration, validate contact-driven axial fracture, insufficient and repeated impacts, glancing blows, off-axis damage, coil retention, freely moving fragment containment, reset freshness, callback timing, force/impulse/energy logging, timestep convergence, and failure controls in the pinned runtime.
candidates.risk: Exact notch strength and tool-handle dimensions are not published and must remain frozen testable assumptions. The inspected images support a representative accessible cavity fixture but not exact CAD correspondence to the outdated STL. Native PhysX may fail to provide stable millimetre-scale impact fracture or fragment behavior; that is a later component-test rejection condition. Early comparison found different central outcomes from automatic center punching (one dent), nail hammering (fastener penetration), blind riveting (joining plus spent-stem disposal), PCB/tile depaneling (supported bulk fracture), and slide-hammer extraction (momentum-driven pin removal). Full fresh catalog, board, team, and six-suite novelty review remains mandatory after selection.

candidates.title: Manually tap the four prescribed M3 holes in an ODRI actuator shell
candidates.objective: Start an M3 tap in each of the two encoder-mount and two belt-tensioner holes, maintain vertical alignment while applying coordinated axial feed and torque, cut through the shell, and reverse-extract the tap without cross-threading, stripping, cracking, or leaving it jammed.
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires four usable through-threads that accept a representative verification screw to the frozen target depth, with bounded axis error and no stripped material, shell crack, stuck tap, or prohibited state write. Partial credit distinguishes a correct thread start, safe partial depth, and undamaged withdrawal. Cross-threading, excessive torque, shell damage, or tool breakage fails the affected hole.
candidates.industrial_value: ODRI's actuator-shell preparation procedure explicitly prescribes manual M3 tapping for the encoder mount and belt tensioners, requires verticality and through-cutting, and warns that threads in the printed parts strip easily.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must establish a thread without cross-threading, coordinate rotation with axial advancement, preserve tool verticality through multiple turns and regrasps, detect rising resistance, and reverse the tool without damaging a relatively weak printed shell.

candidates.asset_plan: Use the inspected shell imagery and, only where consistent, the explicitly outdated historical mesh to author a representative rigid shell fixture. Acquire or derive the exact four M3 hole locations and local wall depths before construction. Implement contact-driven rotational advancement and resistance, with physical tilted-start, jam, stripping, crack, and reverse-extraction outcomes. Validate clean starts, misalignment, over-torque damage, reset behavior, and timestep sensitivity before robot integration.
candidates.risk: The procedure and failure mode are grounded, but the acquired visuals primarily establish HELICOIL locations rather than the exact encoder and tensioner tapping geometry. Local hole axes, wall depths, and material strength remain essential for a faithful interaction. Fine contact-driven cutting may also be unstable or collapse into an abstract screw-coordinate model, and novelty against existing tapping, drilling, and screw-starting tasks is unresolved.

A defensible shell material and thread-damage model

Complete novelty comparison against tapping, drilling, machining, and screw-starting records

candidates.title: Press five bearings level into an ODRI actuator shell
candidates.objective: Identify three 8 × 4 × 2 mm transmission bearings and two 32 × 25 × 4 mm output bearings, place each over its correct shell seat, maintain horizontal alignment, and press it fully into the specified light press-fit using moderate force without cocking or damaging the bearing or printed shell.
candidates.success_conditions: Full success requires all five bearings in the correct seats, fully seated within frozen depth and angular tolerances for two seconds, with no cocked or wrong-seat bearing, excessive force, cracked seat, deformed bearing, dropped component, or direct state write. Safe alignment and partial seating may receive partial credit; continued pressing after detected cocking is a failure.
candidates.industrial_value: ODRI's actuator-shell preparation procedure specifies the two bearing sizes and quantities, describes a light press-fit removable with moderate manual force, and explicitly requires keeping each bearing horizontal during installation.
candidates.dexterity: The robot must manipulate thin rings at two scales, center them over close-fitting seats, regulate insertion force, detect incipient cocking, and stop or recover before damaging the printed seat.

candidates.asset_plan: Use rigid bearing rings and a representative printed-shell fixture. Obtain and inspect the referenced bearing-location images or verified seat geometry before modeling. Freeze unpublished interference, friction, press force, damage, and seating tolerances as prototype assumptions. Component tests must cover free alignment, correct seating, cocking, wrong-size placement, excessive-force damage, removal force, reset freshness, and timestep convergence before YAM integration.
candidates.risk: Bearing dimensions, quantities, press-fit character, and handling instructions are supported, but the acquired visual supplement does not establish all bearing-seat diameters, depths, spacing, or approach constraints. Without those features the task risks becoming generic ring insertion, and novelty against bearing insertion and press-fit objectives remains unresolved.
missing_evidence: Verified bearing-seat diameters, depths, locations, and approach access for all five bearings
A defensible representative interference and damage model
Native press-fit tests distinguishing seating, cocking, wrong-size placement, and excessive-force damage
Complete novelty comparison against bearing insertion, press-fit, ring-placement, and generic insertion tasks

selection_reason: Selected because the repaired evidence now establishes the industrial procedure, four shell-base insert locations, accessible open-cavity geometry, manufactured notch fracture, hammer-actuated straight-mandrel mechanism, M2.5 tool family, retained-coil outcome, and mandatory fragment removal. This is sufficient for a representative rigid-PhysX build and component-test attempt with openly frozen calibration assumptions. The tapping and bearing objectives are industrially meaningful but retain critical local-geometry and physics gaps. Selection is factual readiness only: comprehensive fresh novelty review, native component validation, two full-score real-action YAM demonstrations, controls, replay/portability checks, and the single permitted final Dream episode remain later mandatory gates.
